paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God takes wickedness seriously, and He deals with it. The scroll says it plainly: the LORD of Hosts says the curse "will enter the house of the thief and the house of him who swears falsely by My name" (Zechariah 5:4). Stealing and lying under oath aren't small stuff to Him, and a curse that moves in and stays inside the house is not a curse that's playing around.

Then comes the part that gets me. The angel shoves Wickedness down into that basket and pushes the lead cover shut (Zechariah 5:8). Two women lift it up between heaven and earth and carry it off to Shinar (Zechariah 5:9-11). I think that's the comfort tucked inside the scary part, baker: wickedness doesn't get the last word, because God is the One in charge of it, and He has somewhere to put it. Now THAT'S a lid I'm glad I'm not under.

So what do we bake with this? We take our own honesty seriously, even in the small stuff, because God sees every house. And we rest easy, because the God who sent that scroll is still dealing with wickedness in all the land (Zechariah 5:3). Zechariah's night isn't over yet, friend, so keep that oven warm.
